title: Agora: Toward Autonomous Bug Detection in Production-Level Consensus Protocols with LLM Agents
claim: Baseline agents only catch low-level bugs; a role-separated multi-agent system with memory and a test-refinement loop finds deep logic bugs.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right: baseline loop, input/results bar charts, multi-agent architecture
description: The figure has three dashed-border panels. On the left, a Baseline panel shows a simple loop: Reason and Act boxes in green inside a yellow box, then a Consensus Protocol Repo box and a Bug Report box, with a feedback arrow looping back. In the middle, an Input panel (CodeBase folder icon) sits above a Results panel with two small bar charts. Total Bugs: baseline 22, Agora 15. Logic Bugs: baseline 0, Agora 15. Gray block arrows link the panels. On the right, the large Agora panel shows an Orchestrator Agent at the top (Bug Exploitation, State Analyzer), a Strategy Agent (Constraints Analyzer, Context, Scenario Generator) and a TestGen Agent with a Reflection Loop (Generate Test, Run Test, Analyze), and a Memory bar at the bottom (Repo Knowledge, Bug Pattern). Arrows show context, attack scenarios and bugs flowing between agents. Blue, yellow, green and pink fills separate the components. The eye lands on the large right-hand architecture.
caption: Left is the baseline overview. Middle shows the input and result comparison where baselines could only detect low-level implementation bugs, but \consensustester could detect critical protocol-level logic bugs. Right is the overview of \consensustester, which consists of three agents: \agenta agent, \agentb agent and \agentc agent.
abstract: Consensus protocols form the backbone of distributed systems and blockchains, where implementation bugs can cause data corruption and financial losses. While LLM-based approaches show promise in code analysis, they struggle with deep protocol-level logic bugs involving complex state-dependent behaviors across multiple execution stages. We present Agora, a domain-aware multi-agent framework that integrates hypothesis-driven testing with LLM capabilities for systematic protocol verification. Agora employs specialized agents that collaboratively explore protocol state spaces, synthesize attack scenarios using domain-specific constraints, and validate findings through iterative refinement. This explicit role separation enables reasoning about global protocol invariants beyond single-function code analysis. We evaluate Agora on four consensus implementations (Raft, EPaxos, HotStuff, BullShark) using four state-of-the-art LLMs. Agora discovers 15 previously unknown protocol-level logic bugs that violate safety properties, while existing LLM-based agents fail to detect any such protocol-level logic bugs. Our results demonstrate that domain-aware multi-agent collaboration is essential for detecting deep logic bugs in complex protocols.
